## Description

Mini script to explore output from sensitivity analyses. Can we connect non-linear relationships to mismatches between the qualitative / quantitative models? 

More on sensitivity analysis:
Use boosted regression trees to examine the relative importance of model edges (linkages) in determining the response of a given well-being variable to a HAB simulation in the Status Quo model based on Melbourne-Thomas et al. (2012): https://esapubs.org/archive/mono/M082/019/tree.r

**Reminder:** Total catch and Fishery 1 catch have the least agreement between the quantitative and qualitative models. 


```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)

library(here)
library(tidyverse)
library(magrittr)
library(ggplot2)
library(janitor)
library(kableExtra)
library(cowplot)

library(fitdistrplus)

## custom functions
source(here('R/fxns/prepare.dia.R'))
source(here('R/fxns/impact.ss.R'))
source(here('R/fxns/qnm.sensitivity.R'))

gg_color_hue <- function(n) {
  hues = seq(15, 375, length = n + 1)
  hcl(h = hues, l = 65, c = 100)[1:n]
}

## let's time things
end.timer <- function(s){round(Sys.time()-s,2)}

## read in which version of the data from qpress?
sim.date <- '20240923' ## 9/20/2024 and 9/19/2024 are the same, just run on different computers

```


## Data

Read in each data frame of sensitivity output and combine into one.
```{r}
fit.fish2.df <- read_csv(here('data','qnm_out','sensitivity',paste0('gbmResults_Fishery2_GaussTr5Lr01_',sim.date,'.csv')))
fit.catch.df <- read_csv(here('data','qnm_out','sensitivity',paste0('gbmResults_TotalCatch_GaussTr5Lr01_',sim.date,'.csv')))
fit.fish1.df <- read_csv(here('data','qnm_out','sensitivity',paste0('gbmResults_Fishery1_GaussTr5Lr01_',sim.date,'.csv')))
fit.biomass.df <- read_csv(here('data','qnm_out','sensitivity',paste0('gbmResults_SpawningBiomass_GaussTr5Lr01_',sim.date,'.csv')))

fit.df <- bind_rows(fit.fish2.df, fit.fish1.df, fit.catch.df, fit.biomass.df)
fit.df %<>% rename(rel_inf=rel.inf)
```

separate om / hcr column. clean up om so all are capitalized
```{r}
fit.df %<>% separate(col=name, into=c("tmp1","OM","tmp2","HCR"), sep="-", remove=FALSE) %>% dplyr::select(-tmp1,-tmp2) %>%
  mutate(HCR=ifelse(HCR=="c","C",HCR))
```

add in edge densities of each OMxHCR model.
```{r}
complexity_df <- read_csv(here('data','qnm_models','qnm_complexity_stats.csv'))
complexity_df %>%
  bind_rows(complexity_df %>% filter(MS=="A") %>%
              mutate(MS='D')) %>%
  rename(HCR=MS) %>%
  mutate(OM=substr(QNM,1,1)) %>%
  dplyr::select(-QNM) %>%
  right_join(fit.df, by=c("OM","HCR")) -> fit.df
```

grab just the top 10% influential links for each variable.
```{r}
dat.top10 <- fit.df %>% group_by(Variable) %>%
  slice_max(order_by=rel_inf, prop=0.10)
```


Read in the data and format as for fig 6
```{r}
speciesALL_compare <- read_csv(here('data','results',paste0('mseVqnm_prob-psim_species1-2_allHCRallOM_',sim.date,'.csv')))

speciesALL_compare %<>% 
  filter(code != "2-A") %>%     # QNM 2 HCR A doesn't have a perturbation
  mutate(variable_out=fct_recode(variable_out,"Fishery 1 catch"="fishery_1_catch",
                                 "Fishery 2 catch"="fishery_2_catch",
                                 "Total catch"="total_catch",
                                 "Spawning biomass"="spawning_biomass"))  %>%
  filter(code != "2-A") %>%
  mutate(equiv=ifelse(abs(psims)<60, 'y','n')) %>%
  mutate(match=ifelse((psims < 0 & prob < 0) | (psims > 0 & prob > 0), "match","mismatch")) %>%
  mutate(match_is_equiv=ifelse(match=='match' & equiv=='y','match, qnm equiv',
                               ifelse(match=='mismatch'& equiv=='y','mismatch, qnm equiv',match))) %>%
  mutate(match_is_equiv=fct_relevel(match_is_equiv, c('match','match, qnm equiv','mismatch','mismatch, qnm equiv'))) %>%
  mutate(model.y=case_when(model.y=="MSE-Species1"~'(sp.1) med longevity',.default='(sp.2) short longevity')) %>%
  separate(code, into=c("OM", "HCR"), sep="-") %>% dplyr::select(-model.x,-psims,-prob,-equiv)
head(speciesALL_compare)
```


## Check density influence

How different are the edge densities by variable? (different models may have gone into the sensitivity analysis since the variable result must vary across stable matrices to run the BRTs)
```{r}
fit.df %>% dplyr::select(Variable,edge_density) %>% 
  distinct() %>%
  mutate(Variable=factor(Variable, levels=rev(c("Total catch", "Fishery 1 catch", "Fishery 2 catch", "Spawning biomass")))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x=Variable, y=edge_density)) + 
  geom_boxplot() + 
  ylim(c(0.12,0.18)) +
  labs(x="Variable",y="Edge Density of QNM") + theme_bw()
```

Great, not so different. which QNMs were represented for which variables?
```{r}
fit.df %>% dplyr::select(Variable,OM,HCR) %>% 
  distinct() %>%
  unite(col=code, OM,HCR, sep="-") %>%
  mutate(present='yes') %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from=code, values_from=present, values_fill='no') %>%
  pivot_longer(cols=2:21, names_to='OM_HCR',values_to='present') %>%
  mutate(Variable=factor(Variable, levels=rev(c("Total catch", "Fishery 1 catch", "Fishery 2 catch", "Spawning biomass")))) %>%
  ggplot() +
  geom_tile(aes(x=Variable, y=OM_HCR, fill=as.factor(present))) +
  geom_vline(aes(xintercept=1.5), col='black') +
  geom_vline(aes(xintercept=2.5), col='black') +
  geom_vline(aes(xintercept=3.5), col='black') +
  geom_vline(aes(xintercept=4.5), col='black') +
  scale_x_discrete(position='top', name='') + 
  scale_fill_manual(values=c("darkred","gray65"), name='in BRTs') +
  theme_bw() + theme(axis.text.x=element_text(angle=45, hjust=0))
```

### Gamma

I'd like some kind of quantitative comparison...  fit a model to each distribution of relative influence values.

#### By Variable


are the distributions of relative influence values significantly different depending on the variable?
```{r}
m.null <- glm(rel_inf ~ 1, family=Gamma(link='log'),data=fit.df) 
  
m.var <- glm(rel_inf ~ Variable, family=Gamma(link='log'),data=fit.df)

m.var2 <- glm(rel_inf ~ Variable+edge_density, family=Gamma(link='log'),data=fit.df)

m.var3 <- glm(rel_inf ~ Variable*edge_density, family=Gamma(link='log'),data=fit.df)

summary(m.var)
anova(m.null, m.var, m.var2, m.var3, test = "LRT")
```
<!-- Call: -->
<!-- glm(formula = rel_inf ~ Variable, family = Gamma, data = fit.df) -->

<!-- Coefficients: -->
<!--                           Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|)     -->
<!-- (Intercept)               0.653750   0.062275  10.498   <2e-16 *** -->
<!-- VariableFishery 2 catch  -0.006058   0.092775  -0.065    0.948     -->
<!-- VariableSpawning biomass  0.003750   0.108070   0.035    0.972     -->
<!-- VariableTotal catch      -0.012321   0.082324  -0.150    0.881     -->
<!-- --- -->
<!-- Signif. codes:  0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1 -->

<!-- (Dispersion parameter for Gamma family taken to be 9.491792) -->

<!--     Null deviance: 8890.6  on 3760  degrees of freedom -->
<!-- Residual deviance: 8890.3  on 3757  degrees of freedom -->
<!-- AIC: 9621 -->

<!-- Number of Fisher Scoring iterations: 9 -->


<!-- Analysis of Deviance Table -->

<!-- Model 1: rel_inf ~ 1 -->
<!-- Model 2: rel_inf ~ Variable -->
<!--   Resid. Df Resid. Dev Df Deviance Pr(>Chi) -->
<!-- 1      3760     8890.6        -->              
<!-- 2      3757     8890.3  3  0.33109   0.9983 -->

```{r}
set.seed(55)
test.fit <- fitdist(data=fit.df$rel_inf, distr='gamma', method = "mle")
summary(test.fit)
coef(test.fit)
```

```{r}
set.seed(55)

fit.nested <- fit.df %>%
  dplyr::select(Variable,rel_inf) %>%
  group_by(Variable) %>%
  nest() %>%
  mutate(my_gamma = map(data, function(x) (fitdist(data=x$rel_inf, distr='gamma', method = "mle")))) %>%
  mutate(shape=map(data, function(x) (x[[1]][1])),
         rate=map(data, function(x) (x[[1]][2])))

fits.gamma <- fit.nested %>% dplyr::select(Variable, shape, rate) %>% unnest(cols=c(shape, rate)) %>%
   mutate(Variable=factor(Variable, levels=c("Total catch", "Fishery 1 catch", "Fishery 2 catch", "Spawning biomass"))) %>%
  arrange(Variable)
fits.gamma
```



```{r}

ggplot(aes(x=rel_inf)) +
  geom_histogram(aes(y = ..density.., group=1, fill=Variable)) +
  geom_text(aes(x = 60, y = 0.3, label = paste0('\U03B1: ',round(shape,2))), size=4, hjust=1) +
```

### compare to mismatches

I had a theory that variables with greater spread of relative influence values in a given OM/HCR would be more likely to have a mismatch between the qual / quant models in that particular OM/HCR. I don’t think this is supported by the data.

merge data sets.
```{r}
fits_v_match <- fits.gamma2 %>%
  mutate(HCR=ifelse(HCR=="c","C",HCR)) %>%
  left_join(speciesALL_compare, by=c("Variable"="variable_out","OM","HCR"))
```


```{r}
fits_v_match %>%
  pivot_longer(cols=c(shape, rate), names_to="parameters",values_to="value") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x=match_is_equiv, y=value))+
  geom_boxplot() +
  facet_grid(cols=vars(parameters)) +
  labs(x='qual v quant response',y='') +
  theme_bw() + theme(axis.text.x=element_text(angle=45,hjust=1))

fits_v_match %>%
  pivot_longer(cols=c(shape, rate), names_to="parameters",values_to="value") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x=match, y=value))+
  geom_boxplot() +
  facet_grid(cols=vars(parameters)) +
  labs(x='qual v quant response',y='') +
  theme_bw() + theme(axis.text.x=element_text(angle=45,hjust=1))
```

```{r}
fits_v_match %>%
  dplyr::select(-match_is_equiv) %>%
   pivot_longer(cols=c(shape, rate), names_to="parameters",values_to="value") %>%
  group_by(Variable,OM,operating_model,model.y,parameters) %>%
  mutate(n_compare=n()) %>%

  summarise(mean_param=mean(value), n_match=n()) %>%

    labs(subtitle="(sp.1) med longevity", title="Gamma Parameters v. Matches") + theme_bw()
```

## Link identity

Which specific links were most influential?

```{r}
p <- 0.075
fit_by_VOM <- fit.df %>%
  group_by(Variable,Link, OM) %>%
  summarise(mean_ri=mean(rel_inf), sd_ri=sd(rel_inf)) %>%
  group_by(Variable, OM) %>%
  slice_max(order_by=mean_ri, prop=p) %>%
  unite(Variable, OM, col="Variable_OM", sep="_")

my_heatmap <- fit_by_VOM %>%
  mutate(Link=factor(Link,levels=rev(unique(arrange(fit_by_VOM,Variable_OM)$Link)))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(y=Link,x=Variable_OM, fill=mean_ri)) +
  geom_tile() +
  scale_fill_distiller(palette = "YlOrBr", direction=1) +
  scale_x_discrete(position = "top") +
  theme_bw() + theme(axis.text.x=element_text(angle=45, hjust=0))

my_heatmap
```
```{r}
png(here('data','qnm_out','sensitivity',paste0('gbmOut_relinf_mean_',substr(p,3,str_length(p)),'pLinks_byVarbyOM_heatmap.png')), res=300,height=1800,width=2800)
my_heatmap +
  scale_fill_distiller(palette = "YlOrBr", direction=1, name="Mean Relative\nInfluence") +
  scale_x_discrete(position = "top") +
  theme_bw() + theme(axis.text.x=element_text(angle=45, hjust=0))
dev.off()
```

Dive into Total catch, Fishery 1 catch more
```{r}
p <- 0.10
v <- "Fishery 1 catch"
fit_by_VOM <- fit.df %>%
  filter(Variable==v) %>%
  group_by(Variable,Link, OM) %>%
  summarise(mean_ri=mean(rel_inf), sd_ri=sd(rel_inf)) %>%
  group_by(Variable, OM) %>%
  slice_max(order_by=mean_ri, prop=p) %>%
  unite(Variable, OM, col="Variable_OM", sep="_")

my_heatmap <- fit_by_VOM %>%
  mutate(Link=factor(Link,levels=rev(unique(arrange(fit_by_VOM,Variable_OM)$Link)))) %>%
```

### Compare to mismatches

#### all : mismatches
Dive into the most influential links for comparisons where both Species 1 and 2 were off.

First, grab mismatches in both species.
```{r}
compare_mismatch <- speciesALL_compare %>%
  dplyr::select(-match) %>%
  mutate(model.y=ifelse(grepl('sp.1', model.y),'species_1_med_longevity','species_2_short_longevity')) %>% 
  pivot_wider(names_from=model.y, values_from=match_is_equiv) %>%
  filter((species_1_med_longevity %in% c('mismatch','mismatch, qnm equiv')) & 
           (species_2_short_longevity %in% c('mismatch','mismatch, qnm equiv')))

compare_mismatch %<>% left_join(fit.df, by=c("OM", "HCR", "variable_out"="Variable"))
```


Then check out the top 10% of links for those variables x OMs x HCRs
```{r}
p <- 0.10
fit_by_VOM_mismatches <- compare_mismatch %>%
  group_by(variable_out, Link, OM) %>%
  summarise(mean_ri=mean(rel_inf), sd_ri=sd(rel_inf)) %>%
  group_by(variable_out, OM) %>%
  slice_max(order_by=mean_ri, prop=p) %>%
  unite(variable_out, OM, col="Variable_OM", sep="_") %>%
  mutate(type)

fit_by_VOM_mismatches %>%
  mutate(Link=factor(Link,levels=rev(unique(arrange(fit_by_VOM,Variable_OM)$Link)))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(y=Link,x=Variable_OM, fill=mean_ri)) +
  geom_tile() +
  scale_fill_distiller(palette = "YlOrBr", direction=1) +
  scale_x_discrete(position = "top") +
  theme_bw() + theme(axis.text.x=element_text(angle=45, hjust=0))
```



#### matches : mismatches

Dive into the most influential links for comparisons where both Species 1 and 2 were mismatched VERSUS where either Species 1 or 2 matched. (only one OMxHCR for Total catch had both species 1 and 2 match)

First, grab matches in both species. (we have mismatches from above)
```{r}
compare_match <- speciesALL_compare %>%
  dplyr::select(-match) %>%
  mutate(model.y=ifelse(grepl('sp.1', model.y),'species_1_med_longevity','species_2_short_longevity')) %>% 
  pivot_wider(names_from=model.y, values_from=match_is_equiv) %>%
  filter((species_1_med_longevity %in% c('match','match, qnm equiv')) | 
           (species_2_short_longevity %in% c('match','match, qnm equiv')))

compare_match %<>% left_join(fit.df, by=c("OM", "HCR", "variable_out"="Variable"))
```

How do the most influential links for this subset compare to the influential links for mismatched variablesxOMxHCRs?
```{r}
v <- 'Fishery 1'
p <- 0.10
# re create the fit_by_VOM but make sure p is the same for both. 
tmp_matches <- compare_match %>%
  group_by(variable_out, Link, OM) %>%
  summarise(mean_ri=mean(rel_inf), sd_ri=sd(rel_inf)) %>%
  group_by(variable_out, OM) %>%
  slice_max(order_by=mean_ri, prop=p) %>%
  unite(variable_out, OM, col="Variable_OM", sep="_") %>%
  mutate(type="matches")
tmp_mismatches <- compare_mismatch %>%
  group_by(variable_out, Link, OM) %>%
  summarise(mean_ri=mean(rel_inf), sd_ri=sd(rel_inf)) %>%
  group_by(variable_out, OM) %>%
  slice_max(order_by=mean_ri, prop=p) %>%
  unite(variable_out, OM, col="Variable_OM", sep="_") %>%
  mutate(type="mismatches")

# plot
tmp_mismatches %>%
  filter(grepl(v, Variable_OM)) %>%
  bind_rows(tmp_matches %>% filter(grepl(v, Variable_OM))) %>%
  mutate(Link=factor(Link,levels=rev(unique(c(arrange(tmp_matches,Variable_OM)$Link,arrange(tmp_mismatches,Variable_OM)$Link))))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(y=Link,x=Variable_OM, fill=mean_ri)) +
  geom_tile() +
  facet_wrap(~type) +
  scale_fill_distiller(palette = "YlOrBr", direction=1) +
  scale_x_discrete(position = "top") +
  theme_bw() + theme(axis.text.x=element_text(angle=45, hjust=0))
```
